name: Array Painting
description: You are given an array of $$$n$$$ integers, where each integer is either $$$0$$$, $$$1$$$, or $$$2$$$. Initially, each element of the array is blue. Your goal is to paint each element of the array red. In order to do so, you can perform operations of two types: pay one coin to choose a blue element and paint it red; choose a red element which is not equal to $$$0$$$ and a blue element adjacent to it, decrease the chosen red element by $$$1$$$, and paint the chosen blue element red. What is the minimum number of coins you have to spend to achieve your goal?
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 2$$$).
output_specification: Print one integer — the minimum number of coins you have to spend in order to paint all elements red.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1849D — Array Painting [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
